gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Fitbit Charge 6 can send live heart rate to only one machine or app at a time, and that Google lists Garmin, Life Fitness and Technogym equipment as not compatible with it, while Peloton, iFIT (NordicTrack), Concept2 (latest firmware only), Echelon, Hydrow, Matrix, Schwinn, Tonal, Wahoo, Zwift and Strava are tested.
standout_why: I could read only NBC Select (nbcnews.com, rank 14). For every pick it says just 'iPhone and Android', with nothing on gym-equipment heart-rate sharing or band and charger changes between generations. It even marks the Apple Watch SE 3 as 'iPhone and Android'. WIRED (cited), Men's Health (cited), TechRadar and Tom's Guide all blocked the fetch or came back truncated, so I could not check them. The score of 2 assumes the cited pages, like NBC, don't name which equipment brands are excluded. I can't rule out that they do.
decides: This confirms the Charge 6 as the budget band for a man who trains on Peloton, NordicTrack/iFIT, Concept2 or Tonal, because the heart rate shows on the machine's screen. It rules the Charge 6 out for anyone whose gym runs Life Fitness or Technogym cardio machines. It also tightens two other cards. The Apple Watch Series 11 needs an iPhone 11 or newer (or iPhone SE 2nd gen) on iOS 26, so it is not 'any iPhone'. A WHOOP 4.0 owner moving to the 5.0 cannot reuse their 4.0 bands.

findings.label: Gym equipment and apps that Google lists as tested for live heart-rate sharing
findings.value: Concept2 (latest firmware only), Echelon, Hydrow, iFIT (NordicTrack), Matrix Fitness, Peloton equipment and app, Schwinn Fitness, Spinning, Strava app, Tonal, Wahoo, Zwift
findings.source_title: Share your real-time heart rate with fitness equipment & apps - Fitbit Help
findings.note: Google gives one list for Fitbit Edge and Fitbit Air. The Charge 6 list is the same with Life Fitness removed. The feature uses the Bluetooth Heart Rate Profile.

findings.label: Equipment brands Google lists as not compatible
findings.source_title: Share your real-time heart rate with fitness equipment & apps - Fitbit Help
findings.note: Google lists Pixel Watch 2 and newer as working with Technogym, and with Garmin through Extended pairing. On the Charge 6, all three brands are excluded.

findings.label: Number of heart-rate sharing connections at once
findings.value: 1 piece of equipment or app at a time (Pixel Watch 3 and later: 2)
findings.source_title: Share your real-time heart rate with fitness equipment & apps - Fitbit Help
findings.note: Google says the Charge 6 can pair during the first 2 minutes of a workout. It also warns that sharing heart rate reduces battery life.

findings.label: iPhone required
findings.value: iPhone 11 or later, including iPhone SE (2nd generation or later), with iOS 26 or later
findings.source_title: Apple Watch Series 11 - Technical Specifications - Apple Support
findings.note: Apple's spec page. The charger in the box is the Apple Watch Magnetic Fast Charger to USB-C Cable (1 m).

findings.label: Health-feature limits in Apple's footnotes
findings.value: Hypertension notifications are not intended for people under 22. Sleep apnea notifications need Series 9 or later. ECG app needs Series 4 or later and excludes SE models.
findings.source_title: Apple Watch Series 11 - Technical Specifications - Apple Support
findings.note: These footnotes give no region list for these features. Apple's general note says some features may not be available in all regions.

findings.label: Apple's current watch lineup (Series 11 may be last generation)
findings.value: Apple's page now names 'Apple Watch Series 12, Apple Watch Ultra 4, and Apple Watch SE 3', which require iPhone 11 or later with iOS 27 or later
findings.source_title: Apple Watch Series 11 Technical Specifications (apple.com, now shows current-lineup footnote)
findings.note: The Series 11 specs URL now carries a footnote naming Series 12, so ChatGPT's 'Apple Watch Series 11 $379' card may point to a previous-generation model. I did not open a Series 12 product page to confirm the model or its price.

findings.label: WHOOP 4.0 band compatibility
findings.value: Not compatible: 'No, WHOOP 5.0 and MG devices aren't compatible with 4.0 bands.'
findings.source_title: Can I use my WHOOP 5.0 or WHOOP MG device with a 4.0 band? - WHOOP Community
findings.note: Reply posted 2025-05-08 by user camdenkelleher on WHOOP's own community forum. The page I fetched showed no staff badge, so I could not confirm the reply is from WHOOP staff. The same user adds that 4.0 bands still work with 4.0 hardware.
